The office was quiet, save for the rhythmic clacking of keyboards and the distant hum of the coffee machine. It was "Bring Your Pet to Work Day," and Dave, a mid-level accountant with a penchant for nervous sweating, had made a fatal error in judgment. He had brought in Barnaby, a African Grey Parrot with a vocabulary that exceeded his own and a memory like a steel trap.

Dave had spent the morning trying to keep Barnaby in his cubicle, whispering, "No, Barnaby, not that. Not the quarterly projections. Not the merger talks."

But Barnaby was bored. And Barnaby had been listening.

It started innocently enough. Dave was on a call with his boss, Mr. Henderson, discussing the sensitive acquisition of a rival firm. "Look, Gary," Dave was saying, "we can't just leak the insider trading data to the press. It’s illegal."

From the corner of the room, Barnaby squawked, "It’s illegal! It’s illegal! It’s illegal!"

Dave froze. He looked at Barnaby. Barnaby looked at Dave, tilting his head with innocent curiosity.

"Uh, Barnaby is... practicing his legal rights," Dave stammered into the phone.

Mr. Henderson paused. "Your parrot knows about insider trading, Dave?"

"No! He’s just... mimicking! He heard me on the phone yesterday!" Dave hissed, covering the mouthpiece. He turned to the bird. "Barnaby, hush! Bad bird!"

Barnaby puffed his feathers. "Bad bird! Bad bird! Sell the stock! Sell the stock!"

Dave’s blood ran cold. He quickly ended the call, claiming a bad connection. He grabbed Barnaby’s cage and rushed to the breakroom, hoping to hide the bird among the donuts. But the breakroom was full of the marketing team, who were notoriously nosy.

"Hey Dave, what’s with the bird?" asked Sarah from Marketing.

"Nothing! Just... training him for a commercial!" Dave lied, sweating profusely.
